# XPath expression built from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/xpath-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-643](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/643.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) that is
built into an XPath expression evaluated by System.Xml:

- `XmlNode.SelectNodes` and `SelectSingleNode` (on an `XmlDocument`, `XmlElement` or any node);
- `XPathNavigator.Select`, `SelectSingleNode`, `Evaluate`, `Compile` and `Matches`, and
  `XPathExpression.Compile`;
- LINQ to XML's `XPathSelectElement`, `XPathSelectElements` and `XPathEvaluate`.

The expression is reported when request data is part of it: concatenated, interpolated, formatted
with `string.Format` or appended to a `StringBuilder`. Numbers, enums, values picked from a
`static readonly` allow-list, and values passed as XPath variables through an `XsltContext` are
not reported.

Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and Minimal API
handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files, the body stream, and any
parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or
`[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and the request object itself (`Request.Query`,
`Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Body`, ...).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A quote in the value ends the string literal of the expression, and the rest becomes XPath: `' or
'1'='1` selects every node, so a login checked against an XML user store accepts any password,
and a search can reveal records or whole documents the user should not see. XPath has no access
control of its own, so the whole document is open to such a query.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the title is concatenated into the expression.

```csharp
using System.Xml;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class BooksController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly XmlDocument _catalog;

    public BooksController(XmlDocument catalog) => _catalog = catalog;

    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Find([FromQuery] string title)
    {
        var nodes = _catalog.SelectNodes("//book[title='" + title + "']");
        return Ok(nodes?.Count);
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the expression is constant and the title is an XPath variable that an
`XsltContext` resolves.

```csharp
using System.Xml;
using System.Xml.XPath;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class BooksController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly XmlDocument _catalog;

    public BooksController(XmlDocument catalog) => _catalog = catalog;

    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Find([FromQuery] string title)
    {
        var expression = XPathExpression.Compile("//book[title=$title]");
        expression.SetContext(new TitleContext(title));
        var nodes = _catalog.CreateNavigator()!.Select(expression);
        return Ok(nodes.Count);
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the XPath expression constant and pass request values as XPath variables (`$name`): compile
  it with `XPathExpression.Compile` and give it an `XsltContext` whose `ResolveVariable` returns the
  value.
- Or accept only values from an allow-list, or convert them to a number first.
- System.Xml has no function that escapes a value for an XPath string literal; replacing quotes by
  hand is easy to get wrong.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages
- System.Xml

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files. Request data read
  inside an expression-bodied method (`=> ...`) or a property getter is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class is missed. A controller
  named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check or
  `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method does not, and a variable assigned again
  after a check still counts as checked.
- `SelectNodes` and `SelectSingleNode` are checked on any object in a file that uses System.Xml, so
  the HtmlAgilityPack methods of the same names (which also take XPath) are reported there and
  missed elsewhere. `XPathNavigator` methods are checked on a navigator declared as such or taken
  from `CreateNavigator()` in the same method.
- An expression compiled from request data in another method and evaluated here is missed.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/xpath/xpath-injection.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/xpath/xpath-injection.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/csharp/xpath/xpath-injection.yml`](../../../rules/csharp/xpath/xpath-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.5.
